commits: b6ef959 - bober(sprint-1): revisit ADR-6's fan-out clause — the rule stands, now for a stated runtime reason
decision: InterruptInsideFanOut STAYS a blocking validation error. ADR-6's own hazard (restart-from-top double execution) argues WHERE an interrupt fires, never whether a fan-out branch may host one — it calls the per-branch clause merely unnecessary, not unsound. This sprint supplies the missing soundness argument from the runtime itself.
runtime_evidence: Checkpoint.interrupt is one InterruptRecord|null (checkpointer.ts:247) — nowhere to hold N concurrent pauses.

grantScope carries no branch key and clearScope deletes every key sharing its prefix before a fresh pass asks (interrupt.ts:268,371-375,485) — a sibling branch's arrival evicts an already-granted branch's approval. interrupt.test.ts:794 pins this eviction as INTENDED for the single-scope case; per-branch fan-out is the identical eviction one level down.
resumeMessageId is hitl:<checkpointId> with no branch key (interrupt.ts:332), consumer matches by node id alone (nodes/plan.ts:142-144) — N branch decisions collapse onto one message row.

The failure is concurrency-dependent (serialized at cap 1 a grant may be consumed before a sibling clears it; concurrent at cap 8 it is not), colliding with the byte-identical-at-cap-1-and-8 determinism criterion.
adr6_correction: ADR-6's claim that hitl_commit 'sits at the fan-in barrier' is FALSE for the shipped artifact. hitl_commit's only inbound edge is e-doc-approval from documenter (outside the region). reduce_sprints — the artifact's actual named barrier — is itself INSIDE the fan-out region (its only inbound edge e-sprint-released is kind:'normal', not 'fanout') and could not host a HITL node under ADR-6's own rule either.
consequence: AUDITS CANNOT FULLY CONVERGE. Five of the six undeclared checkpoint ids (pre-curator, pre-generator, pre-evaluator, pre-code-reviewer, post-sprint) sit inside the fan-out region and stay permanently undeclarable. Only the sixth, out-of-region id remains open. spec feat-1 and feat-3 amended accordingly — audits joins history as recommended for permanent acceptance, now with a runtime-verified reason.
for_sprint_3: Read sprint 3's contract but did NOT edit it — its own sc-3-1/sc-3-4/stopConditions[0] already anticipate this ('subject to whatever sprint 1's ADR permits... amend the spec's audits goal rather than forcing it'). Sprint 3 should declare the one out-of-region id, name the other five as undeclarable citing this ADR, and treat sc-3-4 as met only in the amended sense.
honest_limitation_sc_1_4: Because the rule was NOT relaxed, the 'now legal' test pins the ADR-affirmed-sound shape (HITL on the join, outside the region) rather than a topology that moved illegal->legal — that shape was already legal under ADR-6. Verified transparently: reverting validate.ts leaves that test passing and breaks only the still-forbidden test. Chose this over constructing an artificial newly-legal shape that would not reflect the actual decision.
